title: Granite Ridge Pass Accounts: The Day the Count of Instalments Fallen Due Runs From
content:
On a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass account carrying an instalment schedule, the day from which the instalments that have fallen due are counted is fixed by the position of the plan against the season and by what the pass account shows cleared. The points below set out how the collective answers that question.

*Where the instalment plan was opened before the day the season opened and the pass account shows at least one scheduled instalment already cleared, what are the instalments that have fallen due?* They are the whole months between the day the instalment plan was opened and the handling date, capped at the number of instalments the schedule holds.

*Where the instalment plan was opened on or after the day the season opened?* They are the whole months between the day the pass became scannable and the handling date, capped at the number of instalments the schedule holds.

*And in any other case?* The day the count runs from is not moved by this rule.

*Which condition is read first where a plan was opened before the season opened but nothing has cleared?* Neither of the two conditions is met: the first requires at least one scheduled instalment cleared on the pass account, and the second requires the plan to have been opened on or after the day the season opened.

*Is the cap the same on both?* Yes. On either condition the figure is capped at the number of instalments the schedule holds for that tier.

*Worked on hypothetical dates.* A tier whose schedule holds 6 instalments and whose season opened on 20 November. The plan was opened on 2 October and the pass account shows one scheduled instalment cleared; on a handling date of 20 February the whole months from 2 October number 4, below the cap of 6, so 4 instalments have fallen due.

*And where the same plan was opened on 5 December, after the season opened?* The count runs instead from the day the pass became scannable. On a pass that became scannable on 10 December, the whole months to 20 February number 2.
